title: EFFACT: A Highly Efficient Full-Stack FHE Acceleration Platform
problem: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) suffers from massive ciphertext expansion (thousands of times over plaintext) and enormous off-chip memory bandwidth demands during bootstrapping and privacy-preserving ML inference, making it impractically slow on existing hardware.
motivation: FHE enables secure computation on encrypted data but its ciphertext blowup and compute intensity make practical deployment infeasible without specialized hardware that balances programmability, efficiency, and low area overhead.
method: EFFACT combines a compiler with comprehensive optimizations and vector-friendly hardware targeting both FPGA and ASIC. Key mechanisms include: (1) a streaming memory access scheme that achieves high throughput with limited on-chip SRAM by overlapping data movement with computation; (2) a circuit-level function unit reuse scheme that reduces computing resources without performance loss; (3) novel NTT (Number Theoretic Transform) and automorphism hardware units designed for cost-sensitive architectures. An ISA and compiler backend support multiple FHE schemes (CKKS, BGV, BFV), and design space exploration determines optimal SRAM sizing.
key_novelty: A streaming memory access optimization that enables high NTT throughput with limited on-chip SRAM by exploiting the sequential access pattern of FHE kernels, combined with a circuit-level function unit reuse scheme.
contributions: Streaming memory access scheme enabling high throughput with small SRAM for FHE workloads
Circuit-level function unit reuse that reduces hardware area without performance degradation
Novel NTT and automorphism units optimized for area-cost-sensitive implementations
Full-stack design with ISA and compiler supporting CKKS, BGV, and BFV in both FPGA and ASIC versions

metrics.speedup: FPGA version 1.22x geomean over SOTA FPGA FHE accelerators; ASIC shows improved performance per chip area and performance per Watt vs SOTA ASIC works

limitations: Exact ASIC quantitative improvements and specific baseline names are not given in the abstract.
